subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which identity should be authoritative for implicit approval buttons in QQBot C2C conversations when execApprovals is absent?
rationale: C2C isolation does not identify the bot owner, while restoring button usability without a trusted identity can grant approval authority to every sender admitted by open DM policy.

options.title: Use explicit command authorization
options.body: Keep the merged fallback gate and require a non-wildcard authorized sender or configured approver for direct and group callbacks.

options.title: Add a paired owner identity
options.body: Define and persist a QQBot owner or pairing identity, then allow direct callbacks only when user_openid matches it.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Accept that any sender admitted by open DM policy may approve privileged requests originating in that sender's direct session.

recommendation.title: Use explicit command authorization
recommendation.body: Keep the merged fallback gate and require a non-wildcard authorized sender or configured approver for direct and group callbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged-history trail identifies this person as the merger and recent contributor on the QQBot approval authorization boundary.
